/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 20 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2671 (-81)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3889 (-208)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2227 (-21)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1738 (1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 901 (-2)
CAPESIZE
The market made a sluggish start to the week, with sentiment softening across both the Pacific and Atlantic basins as trading activity remained subdued and fresh enquiry proved limited. The BCI 182 5TC declined by $1,885 to $35,271. The C5 index fell by 0.759 to $11.045, while the C3 index eased by 0.612 to $32.105. In the Pacific conditions weakened amid a lack of fresh demand. Only one major miner was active alongside a couple of operator-controlled cargoes, resulting in a thinly traded session. Fixtures were reported at $11.00 to $11.05 on C5, with little indication of any upward momentum as the market searched for direction. The Atlantic also experienced a quieter day, with owners seemingly adopting a wait-and-see approach rather than chasing the limited enquiry available. Activity remained sparse, although reports emerged that $32.00 was concluded late on Friday for a C3 cargo on index dates, broadly setting the tone for today’s softer market.
PANAMAX
The market has taken on a typical Monday feel with activity remaining subdued following the bearish sentiment that emerged towards the end of last week. Brokers have reported a quiet start to the week with limited fresh enquiry for both trans Atlantic and fronthaul cargoes. That said, some market participants suggest the tonnage list is beginning to tighten, particularly in the North Continent. Market sources indicate that both Owners and Charterers are adopting a cautious wait-and-see approach as they look to gauge the likely direction of the market over the coming days. With sentiment still uncertain participants appear reluctant to commit too early, preferring instead to monitor cargo volumes and broader market developments. The Pacific is showing a similar trend. While brokers report of fresh mineral cargoes emerging from Indonesia and Australia, activity remains measured for now. Both Owners and Charterers are said to be reassessing their positions and subsequently their rate ideas, choosing to take stock of market conditions before making any significant commitments. This uncertainty was reflected in the P5TC, which declined by $191 today to settle at $20,045.
SUPRAMAX
After last week closed with a very quiet Friday, this week started in the same vein with minimal reported trades. The 11TC average saw a slight increase of $5 to start the week at $21,965, with the biggest mover being the fronthaul from Canakkale route S1B, as the limited tonnage list mentioned last week continued. Otherwise there were minor movements with the Asian market remaining positive, which is still being off set by a correction in the North American levels. Fundamentals appear unchanged, so hopefully with the World Cup over, activity will improve as the week goes on. The Cl Yingna He (63,126 2021) prompt in Nansha was said to have fixed short period with Drydel at $22,500, although the duration was elusive, and an Ultramax open in East Coast India was rumoured to have agreed $13,000 for a trip to US Gulf with steels, but no further details emerged.
HANDYSIZE
A quiet start to the week with the BHSI closing at 901 while the 7TC average slipped by $37 to settle at $16,224. In the Continent and Mediterranean only minor fluctuations were recorded, and the market appeared broadly balanced, with rates slightly above previous levels. By contrast activity in the US Gulf and South Atlantic remained limited, with rates continuing to follow a slight downward trend. The Asian market also experienced a quiet day with the tonnage list appearing slightly longer and Charterers beginning to mark rates lower.

Atlantic
The Norse Bornholm (39,556 2026) open Houston 20 July was fixed for a trip down to Upriver, while the Sirius (37,705 2011) open NC South America was heard fixed to the East Mediterranean with scrap in the low $20,000's, although further details were not disclosed. From EC South America the T Prime (32,451 2011) open Rio Grande was reported fixed from Recalada to China with petcoke at around $20,000, with some sources suggesting $21,500 by Oldendorff, although full details were not confirmed. Additionally a small Handy was heard to have fixed for a trip delivery Recalada to N Brazil with grains at $16,500 by Lauritzen, but other details were not confirmed.

Asia
The TSL Lusaha (35,947 2015) open Dalian 20–25 July was heard fixed to Taiwan at $18,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Fenix secures approvals for Beebyn-W10

Australian miner Fenix Resources has won final regulatory approvals for its 2.4-3 Mtpa Beebyn-W10 iron ore mine, part of the Weld Range project in Western Australia, with first production due this quarter and first shipment set for Q4, the company said on 20 July.

Beebyn-W10 sits alongside Fenix's 1.5 Mtpa Beebyn-W11 mine, which shipped first ore in August 2025, together forming the Beebyn hub. The hub will offset depleting output from Fenix's Iron Ridge and Shine mines, the firm said in its December 2025 three-year plan. Fenix is targeting total production of 5.4-6 Mtpa in 2027-28, up from 4.2-4.8 Mtpa in 2025-26, with Beebyn-W11 ramping to 3 Mtpa and Beebyn-W10 filling the remaining 2.4-3 Mtpa. Weld Range holds an estimated 290 Mt at 56.8% Fe and 99 Mt >58% Fe.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
The front of the Cape FFA curve was under significant pressure today, while the back end remained relatively supported. The Aug contract lost the most value with 30750 sold, followed but the Jul and Sep with 33700 and 33900 sold respectively. The Aug v Sep roll widened and weakened today down to -3100. Meanwhile the buy side interest in Q4 was unphased buy the sell-off on the front, with 34500 being paid. Similarly, the Cal27 traded up to a high of 28650 and Cal28 24700 but in limited volume.

PMX
Pmx paper saw persistent selling pressure over the day, though volumes were on the lighter side. the July traded 19,800 - 20,000, with most volume around 19,900. August was the most active contract, dealing across a wide 18,850–19,500 range, though most activity was concentrated between 19,000–19,400 before easing to 18,850 late in the session. ai_analysis.summary: 2026年7月20日波罗的海干散货指数持续走弱，BDI下跌81点至2671，各船型市场表现分化。海峡型领跌（BCI -208至3889），巴拿马型维持偏弱（P5TC -191至20045美元），超灵便型微升（+5至21965美元），灵便型小幅回落。市场整体交投清淡，货盘稀缺，租家与船东均采取观望态度，FFA曲线前端承压明显，后端相对持稳。

sections.title: 市场结构
sections.content: 海峡型C5西澳至青岛航线跌至11.045美元，C3巴西矿至欧洲航线32.105美元，市场情绪偏软。巴拿马型太平洋地区货盘有限，北大洲船舶供应收紧。超灵便型亚洲市场维持正向，抵消北美回调，S1B逆势上扬410点。灵便型大西洋与太平洋市场活动均显清淡，租家开始压价。

sections.title: 干散货信号
sections.content: FFA远期合约全线走弱，海峡型8月合约大跌1400美元至30800-31000，反映短期看跌情绪。巴拿马型8月合约跌700美元至18750-18950，9月前移仓活跃。超灵便型8月合约区间19000-19400。实物市场需关注铁矿石价格及中国钢厂采购节奏，8月前需求能否回暖为关键。

sections.title: 交易重点
sections.content: 关注海峡型C3/C5价差收窄机会。巴拿马型P5TC在20000美元关口获得支撑，Q4及Cal27合约较现货贴水，提供防御性配置空间。超灵便型S1B航线强势或可延续，关注印尼至中国货盘释放。灵便型大西洋基本面偏弱，亚洲市场船舶供应略有过剩。

market_watch: BDI关键支撑2650，若持续失守或引发技术性抛盘
FFA曲线前压力度，8月合约贴水扩大显示短期看淡
铁矿石现货价格走势，钢厂补库节奏决定旺季需求
巴拿马型北大洲可用运力收紧程度及对租金支撑
超灵便型印尼煤炭货盘及S1B强势能否持续

route_focus.view: C3航线报32.105美元，下跌0.612美元，大西洋市场清淡拖累，关注32美元整数关口支撑，短期偏弱整理为主。
P1A_82大西洋至远东航线承压，8月FFA贴水扩大至约700美元，货盘稀缺叠加运力充足，租金仍有下行压力。
Skaw-Passero至里约热内卢航线小涨50美元至8479美元，欧元区煤炭进口需求支撑，短期窄幅震荡。
